messages:
jane_support: FYI customer ACME opened an escalation — p95/p99 latency regressed after last weekend's runtime changes. They report streaming endpoints (chat/streaming generate) show very slow first-byte (TTFB) bursts for some requests, but non-streaming total-time looks similar. Repro steps below.

jane_support: Repro steps we used:
```
# streaming (curl, expect multiple chunks)
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4x-mini","stream":true,"input":"long prompt to trigger streaming"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
\n# non-streaming
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4x-mini","stream":false,"input":"same prompt"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

jane_support: Observed: streaming TTFB often 300-800ms higher at p99 vs non-streaming total time. p95 also increased ~120ms. Attaching sample headers/log excerpt below.

jane_support: sample response headers (streaming request):
```
HTTP/2 200
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-request-id: abc-123
x-coalesce-window-ms: 50
```

jane_support: server logs show batches being held then flushed together: `batcher.flush_delay_ms=50`, but we also see occasional `flush_queue_backpressure` events.

oscar_runtime: digging in runtime — thanks for the repro. Two quick hypotheses: 1) runtime batching/coalescing window increased effective TTFB when KV cache misses + small token emission; 2) edge/proxy (envoy/nginx) HTTP/2 flow-control + kernel TCP cwnd interplay causing chunk coalescing at transport layer.

oscar_runtime: The runtime uses a 50ms coalesce window to group small token outputs for efficiency. Normally that's fine because streaming clients consume continuously, but if client read is delayed (or proxy delays flush) those small emissions get coalesced into a bigger flush later -> increases perceived TTFB.

oscar_runtime: Can you paste full curl --trace output, @jane_support? Need to know whether the client is reading or there's an intermediate buffer.

jane_support: pasted trace to thread, but also customer says their platform (serverless function) proxies calls through an internal HTTP/2 proxy that sometimes uses read buffering.

devon_infra: @oscar_runtime + @jane_support — we've seen envoys with default h2 settings that aggressively buffer for performance under high concurrency. Two knobs to watch: `max_concurrent_streams` and `initial_window_size` / `stream_window_size`. Also some front-door load balancers coalesce small writes to reduce PPS.

devon_infra: Quick test to rule out our runtime: I deployed a debug route that disables coalescing and forces immediate flush. Deploy-bot: started canary 2026-03-14T04:12Z for `no-coalesce` flag on hosted-runtime-2.

deploy-bot: canary deploy `no-coalesce` started on 3 hosts in us-west-2 (task ids t-234,t-235,t-236).

jess_sre: Running synthetic from us-west to their infra: streaming TTFB p99 dropped from 780ms -> 160ms with `no-coalesce` on the canary. Non-streaming total time unchanged. This strongly implicates our coalesce/flush behavior. :eyes:

oscar_runtime: Good signal. That means when we emit small tokens, our 50ms window is delaying first chunk until coalesced. We used 50ms as a conservative perf/cost trade-off; but for some workloads and clients it hurts TTFB.

oscar_runtime: Quick mitigation options:
- reduce coalesce window for streaming routes to 5-10ms
- add adaptive flush: if first token is ready and downstream RTT > threshold, do immediate flush for first N tokens
- provide per-customer header override: `x-redwood-flush-mode: immediate|coalesce`
- fallback to non-streaming for customers highly sensitive to TTFB (server-side decision)

jane_support: Customer asks for immediate mitigation — they can accept a config toggle on their tenant to disable coalescing for streaming. Can we do a hot-toggle?

oscar_runtime: Yes — we have a per-tenant runtime flag. I'll push the toggle to ACME in staging and then prod if signal holds. Note: turning off coalescing increases token write amplification and CPU/p99 in the runtime (more syscalls), so we should monitor throughput and costs.

devon_infra: Parallel infra mitigation: we should check if the proxy is coalescing writes too. If we can reduce downstream proxy buffering, combine with smaller coalesce window we get both lower TTFB and bounded cost. I'll open a PR to expose `envoy.h2.stream_idle_timeout` and `connection_flow_control_window` in our frontdoor config for targeted override.

sre-oncall: Add SLO/alert tweaks — create metric `streaming.ttfb_ms.p99` by customer and route; alert if p99 > 500ms for >5min. Also add dashboard for `runtime.coalesce_window_ms` and `envoy.h2.buffer_coalesce_hits`.

jane_support: Did a quick customer test with special header `X-Client-No-Buffer: 1` (their proxy adds this to downstream) and they saw improvement. That suggests client/proxy read side also matters.

oscar_runtime: For reproducibility, please use `curl --no-buffer` and `stdbuf -o0` wrappers. Example we used:
```
stdbuf -o0 curl -N --no-buffer -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -d '{"model":"gpt-4x-mini","stream":true,"input":"long prompt"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate | ts
```

jane_support: Action items agreed:
- oscar_runtime: flip tenant-level `coalesce=false` for ACME and monitor (canary + 10% then 100%)
- devon_infra: patch frontdoor envoy h2 buffer settings for customer-specific override
- jess_sre: add p99 TTFB alert and dashboard panels (by customer/route)
- jane_support: coordinate with ACME for staged verification and share curl reproducer

jess_sre: I'll create the grafana panel and alert. Query looks like: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(streaming_ttfb_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant, route))` and a heatmap for routes.

oscar_runtime: Quick note — adaptive flush implementation (flush-first-token) is already on the backlog; if we prioritize we could ship in ~2 sprints. For now tenant toggle is fastest.

devon_infra: Heads-up — if we lower coalesce window globally, we might see ~6-9% increase in outbound writes and small CPU/p99 impacts. We'll limit to tenant scope and only widen if needed.

acme_custbot: ACME: thanks, ran test. With `coalesce=false` our p99 streaming TTFB went from 720ms -> 170ms. Non-streaming response time still ~ unchanged. We confirm UX improves. :+1:

jane_support: Great. We'll keep this thread for follow-ups. I'll update ticket and post rollout plan.

oscar_runtime: Postmortem notes to include: why default 50ms was chosen, telemetry gaps (we didn't have customer-level ttfb histograms), and plan to add adaptive flush.

jess_sre: I'll link alerts and runbook to the ticket. Next check-in in 48h unless we see regressions.

sre-oncall: Marking follow-up: run a perf benchmark to quantify cost delta with coalesce off vs on (samples at 10k reqs/min).

jane_support: Thanks team. Closing interim loop with customer — will reopen if anything else.
